answer: An agent economy can cap each origin to one attestation slot per epoch, shared by every identity it claims, like pigment from a single tube spread across a spiral of canvases: each fake thins the colour, and no identity reaches the zenith of earning rights until its turn in the shared queue arrives. Splitting into ten fakes does not create ten slots, it stretches the wait tenfold, and slots cannot be bought because they are issued only by the epoch clock, so an attacker pays in calendar time multiplied by every fake while an honest single identity waits only once.
